answer_text: Resistivity is the resistence of a wire of unit length and unit cross-sectional area; it depends on the material and temprature, not on the size of the sample. Resistance R = rho l / A, so a longer or thinner wire has larger R. For the copper wire, A is about 5 x 10^-7 m2. Then l = R A / rho = (0.12 x 5 x 10^-7) / (1.6 x 10^-8) wich is about 3.3 m. That length of the given wire provides 0.12 ohm.
